uncited: **Clipping Cube Widget:** Represented as a wireframe cube with eight spheres at its corners.
**Cutting Plane:** Defined by an arbitrary alignment, acting like a single face of the clipping cube.
*   **Clipping Mode:** Determines the behavior of the volume outside the clipping cube.
**Initialize Clipping Cube:** The system renders a wireframe cube with spheres at the corners.
**Resize Clipping Cube:** The user drags a lit sphere.
The cube resizes non-uniformly while maintaining its axis-aligned orientation.
**Place Cutting Plane:** The user switches the PIP pad to "cutting" mode.
The PIP pad itself acts as the cutting plane.
The user moves the pad to position the plane through the volume.
The user presses the second pen button to freeze the plane in place.
**Render Focus and Context:** The region inside the clipping cube (or on the correct side of the cutting plane) is rendered using standard surface shading.
The region outside the clipping cube is rendered using Non-Photorealistic Rendering (NPR) contours.
This variant specifically utilizes Non-Photorealistic Rendering (NPR) for the context region.
It isolates a focus region using a clipping cube widget (rendered as a surface) while rendering the context outside the cube as non-photorealistic contours.
This approach is chosen when the user needs to see the structural outline of the clipped volume without the visual clutter of full volume rendering.
The clipping cube widget is resizable via corner dragging and defines the bounded region for clipping.

This method was developed for distributed software-based volume visualization in a virtual environment.
It builds on earlier focus-plus-context work [FG98] and integrates with RTVR capabilities for axis-aligned and oblique clipping.
